This petition is listed on a praecipe moved on behalf of the petitioner, claiming that this could be a case for quashing by consent.

Reliance is placed on an affidavit dated 09.10.2024 of the respondent No.2 (first informant and victim) to the effect that she does not wish to pursue the case against the petitioner and that, as per her free will,
she is withdrawing the allegations that led to registration of the subject FIR for offences under Sections 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 as 14_WP5416_18.doc well as Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act, 1959.

sentences.text: Whether quashing by consent on the basis of such an affidavit can be granted or not is another matter, but the situation is complicated due to Interim Application (L) No.23239 of 2024 being filed by an applicant, claiming to be an intervenor in these proceedings.

According to the applicant in the said application, there was another affidavit of the respondent No.2, who claimed that the applicant in the intervention application and others had provoked the respondent No.2 into falsely implicating the petitioner in the present case.

Although a copy of the purported affidavit annexed to the application does not show the signature of the deponent, considering the seriousness of the allegations, on 17.10.2024, a Division Bench of this Court (Coram: Bharati Dangre and Manjusha Deshpande, JJ.) directed the Senior Police Inspector of Tulinj Police Station to look into the allegations made by the intervention applicant and to take appropriate steps in the matter.
3. The learned APP reports that steps were taken in that regard and a report is received from the concerned Inspector.

4. We have perused the contents of the same and we are of the opinion that an appropriate affidavit needs to be filed on behalf of the respondent-State with regard to the steps taken in pursuance of the aforesaid order dated 17.10.2024.
Such an affidavit be filed within two weeks from today.
It is also to be noted that the respondent No.2 is not present in the Court.
5. The learned counsel, having instructions to appear on behalf of respondent No.2, submits that if a short adjournment is granted, her presence can be ensured.
It is sought to be impressed upon the Court that the respondent No.2 voluntarily desires to withdraw all the allegations made against the petitioner without any reference to any other person.
In view of the above, list for further consideration on 22.12.2025, when respondent No.2 shall remain personally present in this Court.
7. List Criminal Writ Petition No.5417 of 2018 also on the said date.

(MANJUSHA DESHPANDE, J.) (MANISH PITALE, J.)
